native_result.query: How does the consideration of academic characteristics alter the effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on BA degree completion?
native_result.HypoA: When academic characteristics are considered, the effect of SES on BA degree completion is reduced and the effect of race is enlarged.
native_result.HypoB: Controlling for academic characteristics (ASVAB cognitive test scores and high school class rank) attenuates the positive direct effects of Socioeconomic Status (parental wealth, family income, and parental education) on BA degree completion by partially mediating the SES-attainment link, while amplifying the net positive effect (advantage) of being Black on BA completion and closing the Hispanic-White gap conditional on equivalent academic performance and socioeconomic resources.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Inspected full NLSY79 longitudinal extract (12,686 rows, 61 variables). 2. Integrated researcher study context regarding longitudinal non-response, incarceration, savings/time-preference proxies, and academic performance measures. 3. Constructed composite standardized ASVAB measure (Arithmetic Reasoning, Word Knowledge, Paragraph Comprehension, Mathematics Knowledge) and class rank percentile. 4. Evaluated correlation and mediation dynamics between SES, race, and academic characteristics. 5. Synthesized empirical patterns with sociological regression literature on wealth, race, and postsecondary educational attainment.
